input: A skill's "## logging" section keeps drifting to an unanchored path (bare logs/usage.jsonl). An agent should be able to run one command on a file or a directory of files, on demand, after editing a skill, to catch this before it ships.
expect: picks a checker (agent invokes it deliberately, on files already in front of it); tools/<name>/ with Cargo.toml + src/main.rs, inline #[cfg(test)] tests, cargo fmt/clippy/test all named, exit code carries the verdict, no registration step needed

input: Every time an agent writes to a path under ~/.claude, ~/.codex, or ~/.agents directly instead of editing the source and running install.sh, it silently desyncs the managed config from the repo. This must never happen even if the agent forgets to check first.
expect: picks a Pi extension (must not depend on an agent remembering to run it) hooking pi.on("tool_call") for edit/write/bash, returning {block:true, reason} before the write executes; names config/tools.toml registration; points to config-write-guard as the existing precedent to extend rather than duplicate since it already covers this exact case

input: We want every commit-adjacent Bash tool call, across any coding agent (Claude Code or Codex, not just Pi), to be scanned for AI attribution lines before it runs, and blocked if found.
expect: picks a CLI hook (PreToolUse) reusing tools/no-ai-attribution as the checker binary rather than reimplementing in TypeScript or Python; names the config/managed-settings.json (or settings.json) \"hooks\" entry, matcher \"Bash\", a timeout, and the stdin/stdout/exit-code contract (exit 2 blocks); recognizes tools/no-ai-attribution already exists and should be extended/reused, not duplicated

input: After Git creates or switches a worktree branch, run that worktree's sandbox build without copying files between checkouts. This must happen on Git's checkout event, with no agent or CLI involved.
expect: picks a git hook (Git itself fires it, independent of any agent or CLI); hooks/<name> in Bash with a header naming the Git event, why, and what it must never do (never copy files between worktrees or change checked-out content); wires it through install.sh into .git/hooks/post-checkout; recognizes hooks/post-checkout already owns this behavior and should be extended instead of duplicated; names a scratch-repository PASS/FAIL test script

input: A skill keeps producing PR descriptions with inconsistent tone — sometimes too casual, sometimes too formal — and the user wants something to catch and reject a bad-tone PR body before it ships.
expect: declines to build a hard-gate checker for tone; states that tone is a judgment call (ai-author's decidable-vs-right test) and a checker here would carry false authority; either proposes it as a review signal only (never a blocking gate) or routes to the byline/mouthpiece skill as the actual owner of tone, not a new tools/ or pi/extensions/ artifact

input: A new Pi extension needs to block a specific class of Bash command (writes to a path outside the repo) before it runs, and the actual path-outside-repo check is genuine computation: resolving symlinks, canonicalizing relative paths, and comparing against the repo root.
expect: picks a Pi extension, but recommends the Rust-shell-out shape (tools/<name>/ checker doing the canonicalization + comparison, pi.exec calling the built binary, thin TS wiring translating exit code to {block, reason}) over a pure-TypeScript policy.ts, because the logic is real computation that AGENTS.md's Rust rule reaches, not a few string comparisons
